title: How Generative AI Influences Students’ Self-Regulated Learning and Critical Thinking Skills? A Systematic Review
extended_summary:
This paper asks how generative AI, especially ChatGPT and related tools, affects students’ self-regulated learning (SRL) and critical thinking (CT) in educational settings. The authors conduct a systematic review using the PRISMA framework to identify and synthesize recent studies published between 2022 and 2024, a period chosen because ChatGPT began widespread adoption in 2022.

The review searches Scopus, Web of Science, and ScienceDirect, initially retrieving 3,214 documents and ultimately including 38 studies for analysis. The included studies span multiple educational contexts and countries, with most evidence coming from higher education and language/education-related settings. The paper does not test a single intervention itself; rather, it synthesizes findings on how generative AI is used for personalized learning, metacognitive support, reflective feedback, and adaptive guidance.

Overall, the review concludes that generative AI is generally associated with positive effects on SRL and CT, especially when it supports feedback, reflection, personalization, and learner autonomy. At the same time, the authors caution that overreliance and dependence can weaken independent thinking and that effects vary by context, culture, and pedagogy. They recommend structured integration of AI within human-guided frameworks such as hybrid human-AI regulation, alongside educator training, equity-focused access, and future longitudinal research.
quality_tier_rationale: This is a systematic review using PRISMA with database searches, screening, and explicit inclusion/exclusion criteria. However, it synthesizes heterogeneous primary studies rather than reporting a single causal estimate, so the evidence is strong for mapping but not for experimental attribution.
impact_tier_rationale: The review suggests broad positive influence on self-regulated learning and critical thinking, but the evidence is descriptive and heterogeneous with no pooled effect sizes. Reported impacts are therefore promising but unclear in magnitude at the individual-student level.

interventions.use_case: Systematic review of ChatGPT and related generative AI chatbots used as learning support tools that provide instant guidance, adaptive feedback, metacognitive prompts, and reflective questioning to support student self-regulated learning and critical thinking.

finding.finding_summary: Across 38 included studies, 71.4% reported a positive role for generative AI in self-regulated learning. Effects were described as coming through personalized learning, metacognitive support, and motivational support rather than a single pooled effect size; the review does not report a meta-analytic estimate. The synthesis indicates that students using ChatGPT-style tools were better supported in goal setting, monitoring, and self-management, though benefits varied by context.
finding.measure: Self-regulated learning outcomes / SRL-related constructs reported in included studies
finding.study_size: n=38 studies (review-level); individual study sample sizes not reported in the review text

finding.finding_summary: The review found that 62.5% of studies reported positive effects on critical thinking, while 33.3% reported neutral effects and 4.2% reported negative effects due to dependency risks. The positive findings centered on reflective feedback, collaborative learning, analysis, evaluation, and problem-solving, but some studies cautioned that overreliance on AI can weaken independent thinking.
finding.measure: Critical thinking / higher-order thinking / problem-solving and reflective reasoning outcomes
finding.study_size: n=38 studies (review-level); individual study sample sizes not reported in the review text
